findings.title: The question summons judgment
findings.claim: The addressed question makes the hearer inspect and judge the restrainer's act before the act's target is fully unfolded.
findings.mechanism: The focus question carries both considered judgment and an attention-directing request; independent evaluative-question parallels and the adjacent forbidding verb turn that request toward the act of obstruction.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening question becomes an invitation to examine the legitimacy of the restraint, not merely a request to confirm that someone was seen.
findings.containment: The ordinary question about the forbidding person remains intact; the judgment frame is bounded to this addressed formula and its supplied obstructive context.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run publication is trusted and directly anchors both focus branches, while the qualified mental-judgment facet and global inference require an explicit boundary.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir konu hakkında zihinde görüş, kanı veya yargı oluşturma.
branch_activations.carrier: The addressed seeing form carries the act of arriving at a considered view about what is before the hearer.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The evaluative question in 107:1 and the adjacent forbidding action give the hearer a conduct to assess.
branch_activations.activation: Those separate cues move the focus form from bare visual receipt toward an addressed judgment of the obstructive act.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The question summons the hearer to form a judgment about the restraint being presented.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not turn every use of the seeing form into abstract opinion; this judgment is tied to the addressed question and its obstructive object.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Muhataptan bir konu hakkında bilgi veya değerlendirme isteme.
branch_activations.carrier: The formula asks the addressee to respond while directing attention to a concrete case.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The parallel interrogatives in 107:1 and 53:19 direct attention toward moral or devotional evaluation before their cases are disclosed.
branch_activations.activation: Their shared question function meets the focus's named restrainer and makes the address an examination of conduct.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Gördün mü becomes a summons to consider and answer for what the restrainer is doing.
branch_activations.boundary: The formula's attention-and-response force is retained; no complete legal verdict is supplied by this ayah alone.

findings.title: Restraint turned against its proper work
findings.claim: The one who forbids worship makes the capacity meant to restrain wrongdoing serve an inversion of its proper function.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb names other-directed restraint; the supplied continuation identifies the stopped act as prayer and places guidance and protective command on that side, while inter-ayah parallels show rightful restraint as prevention of wrongdoing.
findings.reader_payoff: The obstructer's action becomes a corruption of a useful moral faculty: a brake meant to stop harm is applied to the act that should continue.
findings.containment: The direct meaning of forbidding remains the floor; the reason-and-restraint image describes the function of this act in the supplied context, not a universal claim about every prohibition.

epistemic.reason: A trusted publication directly anchors the reversal, while legacy retrospective evidence supplies later prayer, guidance, and gaze context without an independent target morphology record.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir eylemin yapılmasını yasaklama, engelleme veya caydırma yoluyla durdurma.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus verb carries an active act of stopping another person's action.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Prayer in 96:10 and the direct mosque-obstruction parallel in 2:114 identify the action being stopped as devotional movement.
branch_activations.activation: The stopping verb meets a protected devotional act, making its direction and misuse visible together.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The prohibition is heard as restraint deployed against an act that belongs on the protected side of the contrast.
branch_activations.boundary: The finding concerns this supplied devotional context; it does not make the focus verb itself a synonym for corruption.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: kötü davranışı önleyen akıl ve sağduyu

branch_activations.carrier: The focus verb presents restraint as an outward intervention directed at another.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The continuation places guidance and protective command beside prayer, while 3:104 supplies the proper pattern of enjoining good and forbidding wrong.
branch_activations.activation: The accepted reason facet meets the contrast between guidance-protecting restraint and the focus person's attempt to stop it.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The act appears as the right kind of restraining capacity turned against its proper moral target.
branch_activations.boundary: The supplied branch names a restraining faculty and its contextual inversion; it does not diagnose the person's entire inner capacity.

findings.title: An unauthorized endpoint
findings.claim: The prohibitor's restraint can be perceived as an attempt to set an unauthorized endpoint for another person's directed worship.
findings.mechanism: The direct restraint facet meets the qualified endpoint facet of yanhā, while prayer and guidance context and independent endpoint and mosque-obstruction parallels make the imposed limit materially legible.
findings.reader_payoff: The obstruction acquires a spatial shape: it tries to decide where another person's movement toward worship must end.
findings.containment: The direct act of forbidding remains recoverable; the endpoint is a bounded contextual image, not a replacement gloss for yanhā or a claim that every boundary is unauthorized.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication anchors both declared branches, while the endpoint branch is qualified in the registry and therefore remains explicitly bounded.

findings.title: The watcher becomes watched
findings.claim: The person presented as watcher is repositioned as the one exposed to a superior act of seeing.
findings.mechanism: The focus's mutual-visibility pressure meets the later divine-seeing closure and independent observer-reversal connections, so observation ceases to be one-way human control.
findings.reader_payoff: The apparent overseer loses the security of standing outside the scene: the one who watches is also made visible to judgment.
findings.containment: The finding describes a reversal of observational authority in the supplied sequence; it does not claim reciprocal human-divine visibility or add an unbounded doctrine of omniscience.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication anchors the focus branch, while the reader-walk and connection material provide the later gaze relation with legacy qualification.

branch_activations.carrier: The focus seeing form places the addressed observer and the observed restrainer in a visibility relation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The later statement that Allah sees in 96:14 and the observer-reversal connections in 102:6 and 90:7 supply the superior return of the gaze.
branch_activations.activation: The relational visibility pressure meets the closing divine-seeing frame, turning the apparent watcher into an exposed participant.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The human controller's observation is contained within a larger act of seeing that reaches back to him.
branch_activations.boundary: The packet supports reversal of observational position; it does not require that the human watcher literally see the superior observer.

findings.title: The alleged boundary is put on trial
findings.claim: The attention-demanding question brings the prohibitor's alleged endpoint before judgment, so the restraint itself becomes the object under examination.
findings.mechanism: The focus question opens an inquiry and the qualified endpoint facet of yanhā meets the later prayer-and-guidance frame; the connection of question, limit, and directed practice produces one bounded interaction.
findings.reader_payoff: The listener is asked to inspect not only who is stopping worship but whether that person's claimed boundary has any rightful authority.
findings.containment: The ordinary question and direct prohibition remain intact; the counterfeit-boundary implication is a legacy reader-walk inference, not a verdict detached from the supplied context.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk explicitly labels the boundary distinction as an inference; its two declared focus branches and context contacts are nevertheless supplied and traceable.

findings.title: Cessation returns to the restrainer
findings.claim: The later echo of yanhā in the command that the restrainer desist turns cessation back onto the original restrainer.
findings.mechanism: The retrospective walk links the focus verb to the later same-root form and explicitly describes the role reversal: an act first directed at another returns as a demand on its agent.
findings.reader_payoff: The obstruction carries its own reversal inside the wider reading: the person who stops another is eventually addressed as the one who must stop.
findings.containment: This is a qualified retrospective root echo, not a claim that the focus verb already contains the later inflection or that the later ayah erases the direct prohibition.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective reader-walk supplies the exact later ayah and same-root role reversal, but its target morphology is not independently projected in this packet.

findings.title: An endpoint imposed on a guided course

findings.containment: The direct prohibition remains primary; the hdy image is an attributed source image with no independent lexicon branch record, and the endpoint facet remains qualified.

epistemic.reason: The endpoint contact is supplied by a legacy reader-walk, and the course-and-direction branch is nominated without a focus lexicon record; both are retained with explicit attribution and boundary.
